title: irvingella grandifolia
intro: Irvingella grandifolia, commonly known as the Malabar kino tree, is a plant species native to the Western Ghats of India. This tree has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including the treatment of fever, cough, and respiratory issues, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Irvingella grandifolia include its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit antioxidant activity. The bioactive constituents of Irvingella grandifolia include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
